subject: Audit log exports: formats, residency & SLA clarifications
messages:
From: Jane Harper <security@acmebank.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Audit log exports: formats, residency & SLA questions

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Before we proceed to procurement I need a concise set of answers for Acme Bank's security/compliance team so our legal folks can confirm the controls. High-level asks below — this is focused specifically on audit/access logs: retention, export formats, residency, and deletion behavior.

1) Retention: what is Redwood's default retention period for audit logs in the hosted offering? Can this be adjusted per-customer? For EU customers we need data stored in the EU for the retention window.

2) Export capabilities: what export formats are supported (CSV, Parquet, JSONL)? Is there an API to request an ad-hoc export, and can we push exports directly to a customer-owned S3 (or equivalent) bucket in our AWS account?

3) SLA & performance: if we request a 90-day export (typical volume: ~2M events/day), what is the typical turnaround time? Are exports resumable if interrupted?

4) Deletion & proof: after retention expiry, how is deletion enforced and how can we obtain proof of deletion for audit (hashes, manifests)? If logs were exported to our S3, are deletion events propagated to that exported copy or only to Redwood's internal storage?

5) Timezone & timestamping: are log timestamps stored in UTC or in region-local time?

6) Encryption & key control: for exports to customer S3, can Redwood use customer-managed KMS keys?

We just need short factual answers and any links to the relevant docs. If there's a short export spec you can attach that would help.

Regards,
Jane Harper
Senior Security Analyst — Acme Bank
security@acmebank.com

--
Acme Bank | Information Security
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Jane Harper <security@acmebank.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit log exports: formats, residency & SLA questions

Jane —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; I'm copying product (Evelyn) and engineering (Marcus) for any technical clarifications. I've attached a compact export schema CSV and a one-page EU SLA summary.

1) Retention: hosted default is configurable but we ship with a 365-day default for audit/access logs. Yes — retention can be shortened or extended via contractual settings for Hosted/Dedicated customers; Private deployments are fully configurable by the customer. EU-hosted customers are pinned to EU residency for both live logs and retained archives.

2) Export formats & delivery: we support compressed Parquet (preferred for analytics), newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), and CSV. Exports can be initiated via the Admin Export API (POST /v1/admin/logs/exports) for ad-hoc snapshots, or scheduled nightly exports. We support direct delivery to customer-owned S3 (AWS), Azure Blob Storage, and GCS buckets via preconfigured push connectors.

3) SLA & performance: typical turnaround for a 90-day snapshot depends on event density; engineering estimates below but we offer an export window SLA (standard: 24–72 hours for most hosted customers). Exports are resumable and chunked — if an export is interrupted it resumes from the last committed chunk; we publish a manifest with chunk hashes.

4) Deletion & proof: Redwood enforces deletion in our internal index and object store. For proof we provide a deletion manifest (time, scope, and SHA256 digest of retained manifest) and a signed assertion document for contractual customers. Exports delivered to customer S3 are out-of-band copies — Redwood does not automatically delete customer-owned S3 objects (standard practice). If you require coordinated deletion on exported copies, we support time-limited signed URLs or a contractual push-delete workflow where Redwood issues a signed request to your bucket to remove exported objects (requires an IAM role we can assume or a pre-signed delete token).

5) Timestamps: logs are stored with UTC timestamps (ISO8601). Regional metadata includes the region tag for residency mapping.

6) Encryption: yes — for push exports to customer buckets we can use customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP CMEK) — you'll need to grant the export role/delegated principal the Encrypt/Decrypt & PutObject permissions in your account.

Next steps: Marcus — can you confirm expected export throughput for the EU region with a ~2M events/day profile and whether we should suggest Parquet vs NDJSON for transfer time?

Jane — attached: audit_export_schema_v1.csv (field list + sample rows), eu-sla-summary-2026-10.pdf (SLA bullet points). Happy to hop on a 30-min call to run through specifics.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Lead, Enterprise — Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T16:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit log exports: formats, residency & SLA questions

Team —

Quick internal notes from product side to inform Marcus's throughput estimate and the customer reply:

- Retention policy: hosted default = 365 days. We can contractually set retention to any integer days (30, 90, 365, 1095). For Dedicated customers we provide a legal addendum to lock residency and retention. Private customers control retention via config; we expose a deletion API for automation.

- Export mechanics (API): exports are produced as chunked objects (typically 256MB compressed chunks). Each export run generates a manifest.jsonl with chunk URIs and SHA256 hashes. The Admin Export API accepts filters (time window, event types, org_id) and destination config (s3://, gs://, az://).

- Residency mapping: for EU tenancy we read from EU-resident partitions only; exports will not include records from other regions unless explicitly requested. Make sure Acme's PO includes the residency clause to prevent cross-region fallthrough.

- Deletion proofs: Product will generate a signed deletion assertion for contract customers; legal prefers 3 items in that artifact: scope, timestamp, and digest (manifest-level). Rishi, please confirm the assertion signing process (HSM/KMS key id).

- Export performance knobs: prefer Parquet when the customer needs analytics (smaller, columnar). NDJSON is simpler for quick ingestion but larger. For large volumes we recommend S3 push + server-side multipart upload.

Marcus — FYI: please include an estimated wall-clock for a 90-day export at 2M events/day and a suggested default chunking strategy we can present. Also note whether resumable exports require a temporary staging bucket or can stream directly into the destination.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Product Manager — Compliance
evelyn_hart@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit log exports: formats, residency & SLA questions

Evelyn / Ava / Jane (cc'd on original) —

Engineering estimate & clarifications:

- Throughput: for EU region, with our streaming extractor and current export pipelines, a 90-day window at ~2M events/day (~180M events total) compressed into Parquet and chunked at 256MB yields an export generation time of ~1.5–3 hours for a healthy tenant (no throttles). NDJSON/CSV typically takes 3–6 hours due to larger size and serialization overhead. These times assume export concurrency of 8 workers and network egress to an EU-located S3 endpoint.

- Resumability: exports are resumable at chunk granularity using the manifest. We support resumable multipart uploads to customer S3 if provided with appropriate temporary credentials (we create a pre-signed multipart session). If the export is interrupted, our worker picks up the last committed chunk and continues.

- Staging vs direct stream: we can stream directly to the destination bucket using multipart uploads (preferred). For customers that disallow third-party PUTs, we can stage chunks in Redwood provisional storage for the job and provide a signed URL for customer-side pull.

- Signed manifests & proof: we compute SHA256 per chunk and a manifest-level Merkle-ish digest for quick verification. For contractual customers we can sign the manifest with our KMS key (customer can verify with public key).

- Deletion propagation: confirmation — Redwood will not delete objects you own in your S3 automatically. If you want coordinated deletion, we can implement a push-delete step that assumes a narrow-scoped IAM role with DeleteObject permission, or we provide a signed deletion job that you can run on your side to remove objects at the agreed time.

If you'd like, I can run a quick dry-run for Acme's sample traffic (send us a 7-day sample) and produce concrete wall-clock numbers and an estimated egress size.

Attachments: attached a quick sample manifest excerpt in the CSV we already shared.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Staff Software Engineer — Inference Platform
